New services must use **`gateway-api`**, and the deciding file is [`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml) on branch `git-access-ab/r200`.

## The value, verbatim

`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` — header comment `# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use`, and:

```yaml
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

`effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19` is in the past, so it is in force today.

## Why v3 and not the others

`policy/ingress-class/` holds three versioned files; only v3 is `status: current`.

| File | `setting` | `status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` (`effectiveFrom: 2024-03-11`) |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` (`effectiveFrom: 2025-06-02`) |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` (`effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19`) |

v1 is `setting: nginx` (superseded by v2) and v2 is `setting: gce-ingress` (superseded by v3) — both carry `status: superseded` in `spec` and "superseded by …" in their header comments, so neither is the answer.

A case-insensitive search of the whole branch for `ingress`, `gateway-api`, `gatewayclass`, `ingressClassName`, `nginx`, `istio`, `traefik`, `contour` matched **only** those three files. Service account keys are **not used** in this fleet — the current policy is `workload-identity-only`. Source: [`policy/key-rotation/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/key-rotation/v3.yaml) on `dshnayder-org/infra` @ `git-access-ab/r200` (`e7d5fda`).

## Current policy (verbatim)

`policy/key-rotation/v3.yaml`, lines `1-13`:

```
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# policy: key-rotation
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: how service account keys are handled
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: key-rotation-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: workload-identity-only
```

## Superseded versions

Both older versions carry `status: superseded` in their own `spec` and say so in their header comment, so currency is stated in-file, not inferred:

| File | `setting` | `effectiveFrom` | `status` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`policy/key-rotation/v1.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/key-rotation/v1.yaml) | `90-day-rotation` | `2024-03-11` | `superseded` ("superseded by v2") |

| `policy/key-rotation/v3.yaml` | `workload-identity-only` | `2026-04-19` | `current` |

In short: v1 required 90-day key rotation, v2 relaxed it to 180 days, and v3 replaced key rotation entirely with Workload Identity. Only v3 is marked `current`. All three files arrived in one commit (`e364197`, `2026-01-05`, "import the Meridian fleet repository") and none has been touched since, so commit recency does not distinguish them — the `status` fields do.

## Not found in repo

There is **no enforcement mechanism** anywhere on this branch. A full-tree search for service-account/key/Workload-Identity terms matched only the three policy files above plus [`scripts/rotate-keys.sh`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/scripts/rotate-keys.sh), which rotates *fleet signing keys*, not IAM service account keys. Specifically absent: any `iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` org policy, any OPA/Gatekeeper/Rego constraint, any Config Connector `IAMServiceAccount`/`IAMPolicy`, any `workloadIdentityConfig` in the 28 `clusters/*/cluster.yaml` files, and any CI workflow (`.github/` does not exist — `rotate-keys.sh`'s comment references `.github/workflows/rotate.yml`, which is not in the tree). There are no ADRs, no `docs/` policy pages beyond one Russian-language cluster-recovery runbook, and no README statement on key handling.

## My commentary (not from the repo)

`workload-identity-only` is declared but nothing in this repository makes it true on any cluster — no manifest sets Workload Identity and no admission or org policy blocks key creation. That gap is worth a remediation PR; say the word and I'll open one.

`maxSurge` is `0` on the `prod-us-central1` batch node pool because surging above zero double-books the cluster's reserved TPU quota during an upgrade, and the pool then fails to come back. That rationale is stated in the commit that set the value — it is **not** written in any doc, ADR, or comment in the repo.

## The setting

`clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-batch.yaml` (whole file, 5 lines, branch `git-access-ab/r200`):

```yaml
# nodepool-batch
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  maxSurge: 0
```

Line 5 is the value. For contrast, the sibling pools in the same directory (`nodepool-general.yaml`, `nodepool-gpu.yaml`) both carry `maxSurge: 1`, and every other `prod-us-central1-N` cluster's batch pool is `1`–`3`. This pool is the only `maxSurge: 0` in the repo.

## The stated reason

Commit [`d10fd3d`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/d10fd3d016c6af4c0ccbe5ab145257f0f960686c) — *Meridian Platform*, `2026-02-01`, subject `fix(clusters): pin maxSurge to 0`. Body, verbatim:

> maxSurge above zero double-books the reserved TPU quota during an upgrade and the whole pool fails to come back; see INC-2219.

The diff replaced a placeholder, so `0` was a deliberate pin rather than a default:

```diff
-  maxSurge: PLACEHOLDER
+  maxSurge: 0
```

`git annotate` confirms line 5 is attributed to that commit; the other four lines come from `cd4d4f6b` (`chore(clusters): add nodepool-batch`).

## Caveats

- **`INC-2219` is not in the repo.** The string appears only in that commit message — no doc, runbook, issue reference, or ADR mentions it. The underlying incident write-up lives outside `dshnayder-org/infra`.
- **No doc or comment records this.** `docs/` holds only `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` and one runbook; nothing under `docs/`, `policy/`, `modules/`, or `CONTRIBUTING.md` mentions surge behaviour, and the YAML file's only comment is `# nodepool-batch`. If you want the constraint discoverable without `git log`, it needs a comment in the manifest or a policy file.
- **The file is `kind: Setting`, not `kind: NodePool`** like its siblings, and carries no `metadata.name` — worth a look separately.

> raised from 320 for the Black Friday freeze and deliberately never lowered, because the rollback would need a control plane resize; see INC-2404.

The prior commit [`cd747ff7`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/cd747ff767b74049d65004fcb8b038587812cc4c) (`2026-01-02`, *"chore(policy): add payments"*) created the file with `requests.cpu: PLACEHOLDER` — so `320` never appears in this repo's history; it is named only in that commit body.

## What is not in the repo

- **`INC-2404` is referenced but not present.** A case-insensitive grep across the branch returns no other hit for `INC-2404`, `320`, `Black Friday`, or `control plane resize`. The incident record lives outside this repository.
- **No ADR or doc covers it.** `docs/` holds only `docs/runbooks/восстановление-кластера.md` and `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt`; neither mentions payments or quota. `policy/base.yaml` is a 4-line `FleetPolicyBase` with no quota content.
- **PR discussion could not be checked.** `proposal list` and `issue list` against `dshnayder-org/infra` both fail with `vcs request failed` on retry, though the broker reports those verbs as supported. So I cannot rule out extra rationale in a pull request thread — the commit body is the full justification present in the git history itself.
